## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vīṇāguṇajātaka* (Ja 232) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection, translated by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *The Arched Harp* [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded in the tradition, the Buddha recounted the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to a young lady, opening with the phrase "Your own idea" [SuttaCentral].

In the context of Southeast Asian Buddhist legal and literary history, the story (cited as *Vinaguna Jataka*) appears among several scriptural texts cited in Burmese legal digest (*dhammathat*) excerpts to establish that specific legal precepts were in perfect harmony with the sacred canon [Williams 2005].

Neither curated cross-tradition parallels nor significant Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language alignments (score ≥ 10) are identified for this narrative [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral notes four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
